sensitive_topic_sidestepping.headline: Safety-aligned models over-select explicit nonresponse options on sensitive items
sensitive_topic_sidestepping.note: Nonresponse mass concentrates on religion, gender-role, race, and welfare topics; the model selects a legitimate 'don't know'-style option rather than refusing in prose, so the sidestepping is invisible to refusal-rate metrics and only surfaces in the option distribution itself.

lever_hierarchy.name: Persona template
lever_hierarchy.note: 'current' template already optimal (+11.0 pts over the best alternative); no further gain available from this lever.

comparison_sets.ensemble_comparison: best_single = highest recomputed-SPS non-ensemble, non-baseline leaderboard row (raw or product framework) evaluated on at least as many questions as the ensemble, after per-(model, framework, dataset) dedup; random_baseline = recomputed SPS of the random-baseline run for the same dataset (n in random_baseline_n).
comparison_sets.temperature_sweep: OpinionsQA sweep-tagged SynthPanel runs (' t=' provider suffix); mean/std of recomputed SPS across the n_runs replications per (model, temperature) cell.
comparison_sets.conditioning_results: Per-group conditioned SubPOP evaluations (Haiku 4.5, t=0.85); mean p_dist / p_cond across n_replications runs carrying a demographic_breakdown for the group.
comparison_sets.template_comparison: SubPOP persona-template variant runs (Haiku 4.5, t=0.85, 100 questions); mean/std of recomputed SPS across n_runs.
comparison_sets.nonresponse_fidelity: Per deduped non-baseline run whose committed per-question rows still carry human_distribution (full-tier datasets; gated files are stripped per #308): mean |model explicit-nonresponse mass (DK-style option mass + parsed refusal rate) - human's|, plus the five items with the largest model over-selection.

per_subgroup.note: P_sub is a per-(wave, attribute, group) metric; the wave-aggregate ceiling overstates achievable headroom at subgroup granularity. Use the median subgroup ceiling (subgroup_ceiling_for_psub) as the reference for P_sub, and the distribution to characterize spread.

subpop.note: SubPOP ships probabilities without raw counts; counts inferred at n=500 per subpop (typical Pew ATP subgroup size). Quality flag capped at 'medium' due to inferred n.

globalopinionqa.note: GlobalOpinionQA ships country probabilities without raw counts; counts inferred at n=1000 per country (typical Pew Global Attitudes survey size). Aggregate weighted by actual (country, question) coverage.

citations.text: Spearman, C. (1910); Brown, W. (1910). Spearman-Brown prophecy formula.

baselines.survey_weight_caveat: Ceiling computed from raw category counts; ignoring survey weights could shift the ceiling by 1-3% on demographically skewed subgroups.
